props.gloss_en: an animal having difficulty giving birth, and the fetus put out its foreleg and brought it back -- permitted to eat
it put out its head, even though it brought it back -- it is as one born
this is the principle: a thing that is its body -- forbidden; and that is not its body -- permitted
but the limb itself [that the fetus put out and withdrew] is forbidden
for the verse says 'and flesh in the field, a tereifa, you shall not eat' (Ex 22:30): once flesh has gone outside its boundary it is forbidden
the stam's reading: the mishna's 'permitted' refers to the fetus, not to the limb
who is a firstborn for inheritance but not for the priests? one who comes after nefalim -- even if its head emerged alive -- or after a nine-month [fetus] whose head emerged dead
the reason is that its head [emerged] dead; had its head [emerged] alive, the one after it would not be a firstborn even for inheritance
and should you say: there it taught us of a person, and here it teaches us of an animal
for a person is not learned from an animal, since an animal has no prozdor
and an animal is not learned from a person, since his facial form is significant
a placenta part of which emerged is forbidden to eat: as it is a sign of offspring in a woman, so is it a sign of offspring in an animal
no -- it really refers to the fetus; and here too [the mishna's 'withdrew'] is needed only for the place of the cut
the fetus put out its foreleg and brought it back, and afterwards one slaughtered its mother -- permitted to eat
one slaughtered its mother and afterwards it brought [the foreleg] back -- forbidden to eat
it put out its foreleg and one cut it off, and afterwards one slaughtered its mother -- what is outside is impure and forbidden
and what is inside is pure and permitted
one slaughtered its mother and afterwards cut it off -- the flesh is [impure by] contact with a carcass: R' Meir
and the Sages say: contact with a slaughtered tereifa
the stam's reading: the baraita's first-clause 'permitted' refers to the fetus, not the limb
as Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said: it is needed only for the place of the cut; here too [the baraita's latter clause] is needed only for the place of the cut
[if] it brought back a hoof -- eat; [if] it brought back hooves -- eat
the stam's reading: [if] it brought back a hoof -- eat the fetus [not the hoof]
Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak: it is needed only for the place of the cut
R' Shimon: a kalut [single-hoofed] offspring of a cow is forbidden
that is only where it came out into the air of the world, but in its mother's womb it is permitted
and the limb itself is permitted

all were included in 'flesh in the field, a tereifa'; when Scripture specified for you of the sin offering that went out of its boundary and returned that it is forbidden -- it is the sin offering the Merciful One specified, but anything else, once it returns, is permitted
'flesh in the field, a tereifa': why does it say [this]? ... one might think this too [returns to permission]; so it says 'tereifa'
since we find of second tithe and first fruits that even though they went outside their boundary and returned, they are permitted
Rabba: like a tereifa -- as a tereifa, once torn, has no permission again, so flesh, once it has gone outside its boundary, has no permission again

as it is written 'you may not eat within your gates the tithe of your grain...' (Deut 12:17): within your gates you may not eat, but [if] they went outside their boundary and returned, they are permitted
Rav: there is birth for limbs
and R' Yochanan: there is no birth for limbs
what is between them? between them is forbidding the minority of the limb that is inside
[on 'no birth for limbs':] it put out a foreleg and withdrew it, and again, until it completed the majority -- what [is the law]? (has the majority gone out, or once it returned, it returned?)
if you say once it returned it returned: it put out a foreleg and it was cut off, and again, until it completed the majority -- what? (has the majority gone out, or do we require a majority at once?)
Rav Chananya: the fetus put out its foreleg in the courtyard -- since it is a boundary for sacrifices, is it also one for this [fetus]?
Abaye: the boundary of a fetus is its mother
Abaye: then ask about lesser sacrifices in Jerusalem! why do you not ask of them? because the boundary of a fetus is its mother
the fetus put out its foreleg between [the cutting of] one siman and the other: does the first siman combine with the second to purify it from [the impurity of] a carcass?
R' Yirmeya: what is [the law] -- must one be concerned for its offspring?
Rav Mesharshiya: according to the one who says we are concerned for the father's seed, a ben pekua that mated with a full-fledged animal -- the offspring has no remedy
a limb begets a limb, so one cuts it off and [the rest] is permitted
it is obvious that its seed is intermixed
for if so, a blind one would beget a blind one, and an amputee an amputee

the question as reformulated presupposes the offspring bears three prohibitions -- fat, blood and the limb that went out: an ordinary animal comes from the force of fat and blood and is permitted; or do we say two prohibitions, not three?
the sciatic nerve applies in a shlil and its fat is forbidden: R' Meir
R' Yehuda: it does not apply in a shlil, and its fat is permitted
rather: [of] anything [that comes] 'from the force' we do not say [it is forbidden] -- it is permitted
and this is what we ask: what is [the law] -- may one drink its milk?

questions.gloss_en: on 'no birth for limbs': limb by limb put out and withdrawn to a majority -- has a majority gone out, or once it returned, it returned? (raised; the text gives no resolution)
limb by limb put out and cut off to a majority -- has a majority gone out, or do we require a majority at once? (the ta shema at 68b.21 is deflected; no resolution)

הכל היו בכלל בשר בשדה טרפה; כשפרט לך הכתוב גבי חטאת... חטאת הוא דפרט רחמנא בה, אבל כל מילי כיון דהדור שרי
אמר מר: לפי שמצינו במעשר שני ובכורים -- היכן מצינו? דכתיב לא תוכל לאכל בשעריך...
תא שמע: זה הכלל... ושאינה גופה מותר. שאין גופה לאתויי מאי? לאו לאתויי כהאי גוונא?

deflected_by.gloss_en: לא, לאתויי קלוט במעי פרה, ואליבא דרבי שמעון -- הני מילי היכא דיצא לאויר העולם, אבל במעי אמו שרי

supports.gloss_en: ותבעי לך קדשים קלים בירושלים? ... דמחיצת עובר אמו היא, הכא נמי מחיצת עובר אמו היא

challenges.gloss_en: מיתיבי: ובשר בשדה טרפה... יכול אף זה כן? תלמוד לומר טרפה; מאי תלמודא? אמר רבה: כטרפה... אף בשר כיון שיצא חוץ למחיצתו שוב אין לו היתר. תיובתא דעולא, תיובתא

objections.gloss_en: תנן: ...והוציא העובר את ידו והחזירו -- מותר באכילה. מאי לאו אאבר? -- is the mishna's 'permitted' not about the limb?

answered_by.gloss_en: לא, אעובר -- no, about the fetus (= p_mishna_aubar)

objections.gloss_en: הא נמי תנינא: שליא שיצתה מקצתה אסורה באכילה, כסימן ולד באשה כך סימן ולד בבהמה -- this too we have learned

אי אמרת בשלמא החזירו דרישא דוקא, תנא סיפא אטו רישא; אלא אי אמרת לא דרישא דוקא ולא דסיפא דוקא, למה ליה למתנייה כלל? -- if the רישא's 'withdrew' is precise [the limb is permitted], the סיפא follows it; but if neither is precise, why teach it at all?

answered_by.gloss_en: לא, לעולם אעובר, וכדאמר רב נחמן בר יצחק: לא נצרכה אלא למקום חתך; הכא נמי (= p_mishna_mekom_chatach)

objections.gloss_en: תא שמע: ...הוציא עובר את ידו והחזירה ואחר כך שחט את אמו -- מותר באכילה; קתני מיהא רישא... מאי לאו אאבר?

answered_by.gloss_en: לא, אעובר -- no, about the fetus (= p_baraita_aubar)

objections.gloss_en: אי אעובר, אימא סיפא: שחט את אמו ואחר כך החזירו -- אסור באכילה; ואי עובר, אמאי אסור?

answered_by.gloss_en: כדאמר רב נחמן בר יצחק: לא נצרכה אלא למקום חתך, הכא נמי (= p_baraita_seifa_mekom_chatach)

objections.gloss_en: איני? והא כי אתא אבימי... פרסה החזיר אכול, פרסות החזיר אכול. מאי לאו החזיר פרסה -- אכול פרסה?

answered_by.gloss_en: לא, החזיר פרסה -- אכול עובר (= p_avimi_aubar)

objections.gloss_en: והא תרי קראי קא נסיב לה! מאי לאו חד לאבר וחד למקום חתך? -- the baraita adduces two verses (פרסה, פרסות): is one not for the limb?

answered_by.gloss_en: לא, חד למקום חתך וחד לקלוט במעי פרה, ואליבא דרבי שמעון (68b.9: p_r_shimon_kalut_asur, p_kalut_bimei_imo_shari)

objections.gloss_en: אמר ליה רב יהודה לעולא: והא רב ושמואל דאמרי תרוייהו אבר עצמו אסור! (amoraic-memra contradiction; kind svara under protest)

answered_by.gloss_en: מאן יהיב לן מעפרא דרב ושמואל ומלינן עיינין, אלא הכי אמר רבי יוחנן: הכל היו בכלל... (= p_ry_chatat_prat)

objections.gloss_en: ולמאן? אי לרבי מאיר -- איסור חלב ודם איכא, איסור יוצא ליכא (דתנן, 69a.15)
אי לרבי יהודה -- איסור יוצא איכא, איסור חלב ודם ליכא (דתנן, 69a.15)
